newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fugitive German linked to Versace killer arrested.
newsitem.headline: Fugitive German linked to Versace killer arrested.

text.p: The fugitive owner of a houseboat in Miami Beach where fashion designer Gianni Versace's alleged killer was found dead has been arrested in Germany on charges of fraud and tax evasion, prosecutors said on Tuesday.

Torsten Reineck, wanted by German authorities since 1992, was taken into custody at Frankfurt international airport when he landed on Monday evening. He was then taken to Leipzig, about 600 km (400 miles) east.
It was not immediately known whether Reineck, 49, had returned to Germany voluntarily or under an extradition-style police escort.

Prosecutors said Reineck's arrest had no connection with the Versace killing. Reineck was named in U.S. media reports as the owner of the houseboat in Miami Beach where police found Andrew Cunanan dead in an apparent suicide in July.
Reineck was wanted on charges of fraud and tax evasion over two Leipzig businesses he set up. The companies, a marketing firm and a real estate company, later went bankrupt and Reineck vanished.
A European arrest warrant had been issued for Reineck in 1993 on those charges. A total of 37 charges relating to his business dealings were outstanding, authorities have said.
Local television in Miami said Reineck, a German national, also owned a gay health club in Las Vegas.

Versace was shot and killed on July 15 at the gate of his oceanfront mansion in the South Beach area of Miami Beach, about two miles (three km) south of the houseboat's mooring. Cunanan was the prime suspect in the police investigation.
